# Anywhere

> Anywhere is a free, open source (MIT) desktop app for watching and driving many coding agents at once. It runs on macOS 13 or later, with unsigned builds for Linux (x86_64) and Windows (x64). There is no account, no cloud tier and no premium tier.

- The desktop app is Rust on GPUI. A Go daemon, pocketd, owns the terminals, so agents keep running after the window closes.
- It runs ten agent CLIs that are already installed and signed in on the machine: Claude Code (`claude`), Codex (`codex`), Cursor (`cursor-agent`), Grok Build (`grok`), OpenCode (`opencode`), Pi (`pi`), omp (`omp`), fx (`fx`), Hermes Agent (`hermes`) and Antigravity (`agy`). It does not proxy models or resell tokens.
- Sessions sit under a project and a git worktree. Each is Working, Needs you, Done, Failed or Idle; Needs you, Failed and Done show in the sidebar, the inbox, the Dock badge and notifications.
- Diffs, commits and a pull request card sit beside the session. Worktrees are created from a branch, with optional setup commands.
- Board tickets, scheduled automations that run while the desktop is closed, delegated work through an orchestrator over MCP, and SSH hosts (Mac, Linux, Windows).
- The `anywhere` command starts sessions, sends prompts, waits for results and edits Board tickets.
- An iPhone and iPad app that pairs with the Mac over Tailscale is coming soon.

## Docs

- [Run your first agent](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/): Install Anywhere, start Claude Code on a project, watch its status, and review what it changed.
- [Install](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/install): Install on macOS, Linux or Windows, and install the `anywhere` command line tool.
- [The anywhere command](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/cli): Every subcommand, flag and exit code of the command line tool.
- [Supported agents](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/agents): Each agent's command, install and sign-in steps, and the status it reports.
- [Sessions and status](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/sessions): Chat and terminal sessions, access modes, and where each status shows.
- [Worktrees](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/worktrees): Start agents in their own git worktrees, run setup commands, and choose where worktrees go.
- [Review](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/review): Read diffs, compare a worktree with a branch, commit, and use the pull request card.
- [Automations](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/automations): Run a prompt on a schedule, and answer a run that needs you.
- [Board](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/board): Write tickets, start them in their own worktrees, and limit how many run at once.
- [Delegation](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/delegation): How a chat hands work to other sessions through the orchestrator over MCP.
- [Hosts](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/hosts): Add a Mac, Linux or Windows host over SSH and open projects on it.
- [iPhone](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/iphone): Pair the iPhone app with a Mac over Tailscale and get push notifications.
- [Architecture](https://getanywhere.dev/docs/architecture): What runs where: pocketd, the desktop app, the iPhone app, the protocol and the push relay.

## Download

- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/mingo023/anywhere): Code, issues, releases and the MIT license.
- [Latest macOS DMG](https://github.com/mingo023/anywhere/releases/latest/download/Anywhere.dmg): Universal, signed and notarized, updated through Sparkle.
